title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Providing Judicial Guarantees for Deepening the Reform of the New Third Board and Establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Certain Opinions on Providing Judicial Guarantees for Deepening the Reform of the National Equities Exchange and Quotations (NEEQ) and Establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange

Fa Fa [2022] No. 17

To: All Higher People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Certain Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Providing Judicial Guarantees for Deepening the Reform of the National Equities Exchange and Quotations (NEEQ) and Establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

June 23, 2022

Deepening the reform of the NEEQ and establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange are important arrangements by the central authorities to comprehensively deepen capital market reforms, improve the basic systems of the capital market, enhance the functions of the capital market, and support the innovative development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). They are also major measures to implement the innovation-driven development strategy and advance the construction of Beijing as an international center for scientific and technological innovation and a national financial management center. To fully leverage the adjudicative functions of the People's Courts, ensure the smooth progress of deepening the NEEQ reform and establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of SMEs and investors, the following opinions are hereby put forward regarding the proper adjudication of cases related to companies listed on the NEEQ and companies listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange.

I. Enhance Understanding and Fully Grasp the Significant Importance and Overall Arrangements of Deepening the NEEQ Reform and Establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange

1. Fully recognize the significant importance of deepening the NEEQ reform and establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Party Central Committee has attached great importance to capital market reform and the development of SMEs. The Central Economic Work Conference, the Outline of the 14th Five-Year Plan, and meetings of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee have all made important deployments for developing "specialized, refined, distinctive, and innovative" SMEs and deepening the NEEQ reform. Aiming to build a main front for serving innovative SMEs, this deepening of the NEEQ reform transforms the NEEQ's Selective Layer into the Beijing Stock Exchange, thereby opening up the full-chain market service system for the continuous growth of SMEs—"venture capital funds and equity investment funds - regional equity markets - NEEQ - stock exchanges"—and creating a positive and healthy market ecosystem for SMEs. This fully reflects the earnest expectations of the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core for the capital market to serve the development of the vast majority of SMEs. People's Courts at all levels must adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, earnestly implement a series of important instructions and directives from General Secretary Xi Jinping regarding the capital market and SME development, and lawfully and properly adjudicate various cases involving the National Equities Exchange and Quotations, the Beijing Stock Exchange, and their listed or unlisted companies, creating a sound judicial environment for the healthy development of SMEs and the construction of a multi-level capital market system.

2. Accurately grasp the overall arrangements for deepening the NEEQ reform and establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange. Under this reform, the NEEQ's Basic Layer and Innovation Layer, together with the Beijing Stock Exchange, focus on serving innovative SMEs, forming a "progressive" market structure: the Beijing Stock Exchange is established based on the transformation of the NEEQ's Selective Layer; the NEEQ retains the Basic Layer and Innovation Layer listed companies; Basic Layer companies that meet the criteria for entering the Innovation Layer will move up to the Innovation Layer; companies listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange are selected from those listed on the NEEQ's Innovation Layer, and the pilot registration system for stock issuance is concurrently implemented. Compared with the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets, the Beijing Stock Exchange has the same legal status and market functions; its listed companies that meet the conditions for transfer may be transferred for listing on the ChiNext Board and the STAR Market. The Beijing Stock Exchange, together with the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges and regional equity markets, adheres to differentiated development and interconnectivity, focusing on achieving "three goals": first, building a set of basic institutional arrangements suited to the characteristics of innovative SMEs; second, smoothing the role of the Beijing Stock Exchange as a link in the multi-level capital market; and third, cultivating a group of "specialized, refined, distinctive, and innovative" SMEs to form a positive market ecosystem. People's Courts at all levels, based on the reality of criminal, civil, and administrative adjudication in securities matters, must deeply understand the multi-level judicial needs arising from the "progressive" market structure of the multi-level capital market. Through judicial adjudication, they should promote a sound market ecosystem where market participants act according to law and agreements, funds and information flow in an orderly manner, entities fulfill their roles and responsibilities, and legitimate rights and interests are effectively protected, providing strong judicial guarantees for investors to invest with confidence and for SMEs to innovate and start businesses boldly.

II. Proactive Engagement at the Forefront, Lawfully Ensuring the Smooth Progress of the Major Deployments for Deepening the NEEQ Reform and Establishing the Beijing Stock Exchange

3. Lawfully ensure administrative supervision by securities regulatory authorities and self-regulatory management by the Beijing Stock Exchange. The establishment of the Beijing Stock Exchange and the pilot implementation of the registration system involve not only front-end reforms to the issuance and listing system but also improvements to supporting systems for listed companies' refinancing, mergers and acquisitions, trading, and delisting, tailored to the characteristics of innovative SMEs by securities regulatory authorities and the Beijing Stock Exchange. People's Courts at all levels, based on judicial adjudication, must ensure the effective implementation of various reform measures by unifying the application of law and support the development of inclusive finance in the multi-level capital market. When adjudicating cases, the People's Courts may refer to and apply relevant provisions of rules, regulatory documents, and business rules concerning stock issuance, listing, and ongoing supervision formulated by securities regulatory authorities and stock exchanges through statutory procedures, provided they do not conflict with laws and regulations. For disputes involving the Beijing Stock Exchange, parties should be actively guided to first express their claims and seek remedies through procedures such as stock exchange hearings and reviews. The provisions of the Securities Law regarding the protection of stock exchanges' performance of self-regulatory functions shall be strictly implemented, and the principle of exemption from civil liability for legitimate self-regulatory actions of stock exchanges shall be applied according to law.

4. Fully respect the reform practices and business rules of the NEEQ as a national-level securities trading venue approved by the State Council. The NEEQ is a national-level securities trading venue approved by the State Council as stipulated in the Securities Law. As the Securities Law's provisions on national-level securities trading venues are relatively general, the NEEQ has explored, during its deepening reform, a set of institutional systems for listing, transfer, and ongoing supervision that are mainly based on securities regulatory authority rules, regulatory documents, and securities trading venue business rules, adapted to the "progressive" market structure. In the process of fact-finding and law application, the People's Courts should fully respect relevant reform practices, refer to and apply relevant rules, regulatory documents, and business rules formulated according to law, and effectively maintain the order of the NEEQ market while protecting the legitimate rights and interests of investors.

5. Implement centralized jurisdiction over cases involving the Beijing Stock Exchange and its listed companies. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Jurisdiction of Cases by the Beijing Financial Court (Fa Shi [2021] No. 7), first-instance civil, commercial, and administrative securities cases related to the management functions of a securities trading venue, where the Beijing Stock Exchange is the defendant or a third party, shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Beijing Financial Court. To unify adjudication standards, stabilize market judicial expectations, and serve the construction of Beijing as a national financial management center, and with reference to the provisions of Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Jurisdiction of Cases by the Beijing Financial Court, first-instance financial civil and commercial cases involving Beijing Stock Exchange listed companies, such as disputes over securities issuance, securities underwriting contracts, securities listing sponsorship contracts, securities listing contracts, securities trading contracts, and securities fraud liability, shall be subject to pilot centralized jurisdiction by the Beijing Financial Court.

6. Fully implement the various judicial measures from the judicial guarantee opinions for the STAR Market and the ChiNext Board. The establishment of the Beijing Stock Exchange and the pilot registration system fully draw on and absorb the reform experience from the STAR Market and ChiNext Board pilot registration systems, with certain differentiated arrangements tailored to the characteristics of SMEs. When adjudicating cases related to the Beijing Stock Exchange, People's Courts at all levels must enhance the consciousness and initiative to provide judicial guarantees for the establishment of the Beijing Stock Exchange and the pilot registration system. Matters not provided for in these Opinions shall be addressed by referring to the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Providing Judicial Guarantees for the Establishment of the STAR Market and the Pilot Registration System Reform (Fa Fa [2019] No. 17) and the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Providing Judicial Guarantees for the ChiNext Board Reform and the Pilot Registration System Reform (Fa Fa [2020] No. 28).

III. Proactive Action, Supporting SMEs to Grow and Strengthen through Capital Markets with Quality Judicial Services

7. Lawfully support securities intermediaries in serving SMEs' listing and financing. Compared with companies listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, innovative SMEs in the NEEQ's Basic Layer, Innovation Layer, and the Beijing Stock Exchange are at an early stage of development and relatively small in scale. When adjudicating cases involving misrepresentation by SMEs and their securities intermediaries, People's Courts at all levels must, based on the reality that the sued SME is still in the entrepreneurial growth stage, accurately and fully understand the principle, as upheld in the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Civil Compensation Cases for Misrepresentation in the Securities Market (Fa Shi [2022] No. 2, hereinafter the "Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation"), that the liability of securities intermediaries should be commensurate with their duty of care, level of attention, and degree of fault, and avoid a "one-size-fits-all" approach. The provisions of Articles 17 to 19 of the Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation should be accurately applied. For the determination of fault of securities intermediaries serving SMEs, the standard of reasonable reliance after excluding professional skepticism should be adhered to, enhancing the inclusiveness and precision of adjudication standards. The differences in responsibilities between the lead sponsors of NEEQ-listed companies and the sponsors of listed companies should be correctly delineated. In accordance with Article 23 of the Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation, the scope of responsibility of lead sponsors should be carefully determined to prevent excessive blame on securities intermediaries from causing a "chilling effect."

8. Differentiate civil liability for misrepresentation according to the "progressive" market structure. When determining whether the content of misrepresentation meets the materiality standard under Article 10 of the Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation, the People's Courts should respect the entrepreneurial growth characteristics of innovative SMEs. The judicial review standard for their information disclosure quality should not be equated to that of mature listed companies on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, achieving a balance between leniency and strictness: where misstatements in financial statements are caused by accounting errors; where promotional content regarding non-quantifiable matters such as technological innovation and R&D expectations in information disclosure documents constitutes reasonable commercial advertising; and where facts not disclosed in the information disclosure documents are immaterial for judging the issuer's financial, business, or operational status, the People's Courts may, depending on the circumstances, determine that such misrepresentation content is not material, pursuant to Articles 6(1) and 10(3) of the Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation and other provisions, thereby creating a favorable environment for innovation and entrepreneurship by innovative SMEs. Since some misconduct by Beijing Stock Exchange listed companies, such as financial fraud, may trace back to their period of listing on the NEEQ, for such cases, the People's Courts must, considering their information disclosure conduct during the transition through the NEEQ's Basic Layer, Innovation Layer, and the Beijing Stock Exchange, accurately grasp the information disclosure requirements at different stages, comprehensively determine the misconduct and its implementation date, and not arbitrarily extend the time range of the implementation date of the misrepresentation, to prevent the undue expansion of civil liability for listed SMEs. The objective reality that the liquidity and price continuity of the NEEQ market differ significantly from those of exchange markets should be respected. In calculating losses in misrepresentation cases involving NEEQ-listed companies, the People's Courts should not directly apply Articles 27 and 28 of the Misrepresentation Judicial Interpretation but should primarily rely on Article 26(5), fully consider professional opinions, and take as reference the usual valuation methods for investments in relevant industries and enterprises, comprehensively weighing various factors to reasonably determine investor losses.

9. Uphold the "three principles" of fairness, impartiality, and transparency in the capital market to lawfully reduce the cost of financing transactions for SMEs. Smoothing direct financing channels in the capital market is an effective measure to address the "difficult and expensive financing" problems of SMEs. For the listing and refinancing of innovative SMEs, it is necessary not only to open up the multi-level capital market to "help them mount the horse" but also to "see them off for a distance" by adhering to the principles of openness, fairness, and impartiality. In the listing process, for "performance-based valuation adjustment mechanism (VAM) agreements" signed with investors to obtain financing, if there is no explicit agreement that non-controlling shareholders are jointly and severally liable with the controlling shareholder or actual controller for performance compensation, the People's Courts shall not support the investor's claim for joint and several liability against the non-controlling shareholder. In the refinancing process, such as private placements by listed companies, for clauses of a "private placement guaranteed return" nature entered into by investors using their advantageous positions with the listed company, its controlling shareholder, actual controller, or principal shareholders, which confer upon the investor special rights to guaranteed returns superior to those of other shareholders of the same class, thus indirectly raising the financing costs of SMEs and violating the fairness principle of the Securities Law and relevant regulatory provisions, the People's Courts shall, according to law, determine such clauses to be invalid. To reduce the listing costs for SMEs, where securities intermediaries claim compensation from the issuer, its controlling shareholder, actual controller, or others for losses they have borne due to the issuer's misrepresentation, based on agreements in the listing sponsorship, underwriting, or continuous supervision agreements, the People's Courts shall not support such claims.

10. Optimize judicial and enforcement procedures to reduce litigation costs for innovative SMEs. People's Courts at all levels must earnestly implement the spirit of the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Fully Leveraging Judicial Functions to Assist the Development of Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises (Fa Fa [2022] No. 2). When handling litigation cases that may have a significant impact on the continuous and stable operation of innovative SMEs, the courts must fully hear the claims of the SMEs and, in accordance with the law, fully optimize litigation procedures including case filing, preservation, trial, and enforcement, effectively reducing the time and economic costs of litigation for enterprises. Property preservation measures against innovative SMEs should be applied cautiously and in accordance with the law. Where a preliminary review indicates that the litigant's claim is clearly unsustainable, the application for preservation shall be dismissed. Where a party applies for preservation beyond the scope of its claim, the application for the excess part shall not be supported. In monetary claims cases, if the SME subject to preservation measures provides security and requests the lifting of the preservation measures, and upon review the security is deemed sufficient and effective, the court shall grant the request by ruling, and the consent of the applicant for preservation shall not be a necessary condition. People's Courts at all levels should, relying on channels such as the 12368 litigation service hotline and enforcement complaints, establish a rapid response mechanism for resolving issues of excessive seizure and arbitrary seizure, promptly accepting and efficiently handling issues raised by parties; enforcement personnel found at fault for issues of excessive seizure and arbitrary seizure shall be held accountable seriously according to law.

IV. Uphold the Bottom Line, Lawfully and Effectively Protect the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Investors

11. Severely crack down on illegal and criminal activities in the NEEQ's Basic Layer, Innovation Layer, and the Beijing Stock Exchange market. Fully leverage the general and specific preventive functions of criminal liability, strictly prevent "passing the gate with defects," and lawfully and severely punish fraudulent and corrupt criminal activities committed through financial fraud or other means to achieve listing on the NEEQ or the Beijing Stock Exchange, or in issuing securities after listing or transfer. Where issuers and securities intermediaries collude to conceal important facts or fabricate major false content in securities issuance documents, and where personnel involved in issuance review and registration abuse their power, accept bribes, or engage in the transfer of benefits, criminal liability shall be pursued severely according to law. Criminal activities such as illegal disclosure or non-disclosure of important information, insider trading, trading using undisclosed information, market manipulation, and breach of trust harming the interests of listed companies shall be severely punished according to law, with increased application of property-based penalties and strict control over the application of probation. For illegal fund-raising activities under the guise of the NEEQ, or raising funds in the name of "original shares of NEEQ-listed companies" to attract investors without complying with lawful issuance procedures, which constitute crimes, severe punishment shall be imposed according to law.

12. Effectively prevent listed companies and NEEQ-listed companies from harming investors' legitimate rights and interests through bankruptcy proceedings. Since the implementation of the Minutes of the Symposium on the Work of the Supreme People's Court on Hearing Cases of Bankruptcy Reorganization of Listed Companies, the People's Courts have lawfully adjudicated a number of bankruptcy reorganization cases involving listed companies, minimizing the adverse social impact of bankruptcy proceedings on listed companies and achieving unification of legal and social effects. As Beijing Stock Exchange listed companies have the same legal status as Shanghai and Shenzhen listed companies, the aforementioned Minutes shall apply to their bankruptcy reorganization cases. Although NEEQ-listed companies are not legally considered listed companies and their bankruptcy reorganization cases are not subject to the procedures in the aforementioned Minutes, as non-listed public companies, their bankruptcy reorganizations also involve the protection of multiple interests, including those of investors and creditors. To prevent NEEQ-listed companies from abusing the bankruptcy reorganization process to evade debts and harm the legitimate rights and interests of investors, when adjudicating bankruptcy reorganization cases, if the NEEQ-listed company's asset transactions during the bankruptcy reorganization process meet the standards for major asset restructuring, the People's Courts shall strengthen communication and coordination with securities regulatory authorities and securities trading venues, urge the company and relevant entities to lawfully fulfill corresponding procedures, pay attention to the compliance of injected assets during the judicial process, and lawfully punish illegal and irregular acts that circumvent securities regulation and harm the interests of the company and investors.

13. Lawfully regulate the investment advisory services of securities investment advisory institutions for the NEEQ's Basic Layer, Innovation Layer, and the Beijing Stock Exchange market. NEEQ-listed companies and Beijing Stock Exchange listed companies are predominantly SMEs, and the investment risks of such enterprises are relatively high. While lawfully applying the provisions on investor suitability management obligations to urge securities firms to properly control the "entry gate" for investors, the People's Courts must also accurately apply Article 161 of the Securities Law to urge securities investment advisory institutions to fulfill their duties and responsibilities. In adjudicating civil compensation cases filed by investors against securities investment advisory institutions concerning NEEQ-listed companies or Beijing Stock Exchange listed companies, the focus shall be on examining whether the institution and its employees have the qualifications for investment services, and whether they have acted in accordance with the principles of objectivity, prudence, and loyalty to clients when providing investment advice. Where securities investment advisory institutions fail to warn investors of potential investment risks, promise guaranteed returns to clients, engage in the transfer of benefits, or commit other acts that deceive investors in violation of regulatory provisions and industry self-regulatory rules, the People's Courts shall, according to law, order them to bear corresponding compensation liability, effectively protecting the legitimate rights and interests of investors.

14. Further improve the diversified dispute resolution mechanism for securities litigation and disputes. The People's Courts at all levels must earnestly implement and comply with the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Representative Actions in Securities Disputes (Fa Shi [2020] No. 5), fully leveraging the institutional functions of securities collective litigation in deterring securities violations and protecting investors. The achievements of the People's Courts' one-stop diversified dispute resolution mechanism should be utilized, and the important role of the People's Courts' mediation platform in resolving securities disputes should be brought into play, perfecting an organic, coordinated, efficient, and convenient diversified dispute resolution mechanism for securities disputes. Based on the characteristics of the NEEQ's Basic Layer, Innovation Layer, and the Beijing Stock Exchange market, the supporting role of professional forces in resolving key disputes in cases should be further strengthened. Rules for the qualification confirmation and management of expert witnesses should be formulated at a faster pace, and their role in case adjudication should be further enhanced to ensure correct fact-finding and application of law.
